title: HIGH: eraser cutting an angled stroke across a brush LINE deletes one whole side (planar arrangement topology / data loss)
description:
USER-REPORTED data loss. Erasing ACROSS the middle of a brush line/stroke to 'cut it in two' SOMETIMES deletes one ENTIRE side (e.g. the whole right half) instead of leaving two trimmed segments.

REPRO (deterministic, isolated to the planar kernel — NOT the eraser filter logic):
A brush stroke is a CLOSED FILLED outline polygon (engine/brushtool.ts: 'closed filled ShapeDisplayObject outlining the brush width', fill set, closed:true) — NOT a stroke-style line. Take a horizontal brush band x=0..200, y=95..105 (10px thick), fill black. Erase with an ANGLED capsule drag whose two endpoints lie OUTSIDE the band on OPPOSITE sides, e.g. buildEraserStamp([{x:90,y:90},{x:110,y:112}], 6) (start above the band at x=90, end below it at x=110). Result: planarEraseShape(...,{mode:'normal'}) returns ONE fill only, x-extent [0,96] — the ENTIRE right half (x~110..200) is gone. Area 2000 -> 909 (>half lost). The 'sometimes' = it fires only for an angled capsule cut whose long edges cross both parallel edges of the band; clean PERPENDICULAR cuts, slight angles, and single dabs all cut cleanly into two surviving faces (x=[0,200]).

Trigger characterization (all on a 0..200 x 95..105 brush, mode normal):
  perp full-span drag (100,88)->(100,112) sz6     -> fills=2 x=[0,200]  OK
  perp single dab (100,100) sz12                  -> fills=2 x=[0,200]  OK
  ANGLED (90,90)->(110,112) sz6                   -> fills=1 x=[0,96]   BUG (right half deleted)
  ANGLED (90,90)->(110,112) sz10                  -> fills=1 x=[0,90]   BUG
  slight-angle (98,90)->(102,110) sz6             -> fills=2 x=[0,200]  OK
  shallow-diag (80,96)->(120,104) sz6             -> fills=2 x=[0,200]  OK

ROOT CAUSE (localized): NOT eraser.ts's edgeFilter midpoint test, and NOT the 1327 even-odd/union pointInEraser family. The right region simply has NO BOUNDED FACE after arrangement construction — it leaks into the UNBOUNDED face. Proven by isolating from all eraser logic in buildArrangementFromShapes (packages/core/src/engine/planar/build.ts): insert the clean brush rectangle PLUS an angled style-less quad loop (the capsule (90,90)->(110,112) r=3). locateFace((150,100)) returns NONE/unbounded and locateFace((50,100)) returns the only bounded face (or vice-versa depending on orientation) — only ONE bounded filled face results. A PERPENDICULAR cut loop over the same rect yields TWO bounded faces (both sides enclosed). So when an angled capsule's two long parallel edges each cross the band's two parallel edges (four near-parallel intersection points), arrangement.ts's edge-split / next-twin face-extraction fails to enclose the far side — that side's faceInteriorPoint then samples no fill region (build.ts assignFaceFillsBySampling -> fill=null) and it vanishes from planarShapeToShape read-back.

So: bug is in the PLANAR ARRANGEMENT KERNEL (packages/core/src/engine/planar/arrangement.ts insertEdge intersection/splitting and arr.build() face extraction), surfaced by eraser.ts inserting the angled capsule as subdivision edges. eraser.ts planarEraseShape (packages/core/src/engine/planar/eraser.ts ~line 154 buildArrangementFromShapes([shape, eraserShape]); faceFilter ~line 194) is the trigger path but the defect is upstream.

FIX DIRECTION: fix the kernel so an angled capsule loop crossing two parallel host edges still encloses BOTH resulting regions as bounded faces (correct intersection ordering + half-edge next/twin linkage at the 4 near-coincident crossing vertices). Equivalent regression: buildArrangementFromShapes([brushRect, angledCutLoop]) must yield TWO bounded filled faces; planarEraseShape on a straight brush band with an angled mid cut must return TWO fills spanning the full original x-extent (trim only the eraser bite, keep both sides). Distinct from 1322 (kernel retired-half-edge guard) and 1327 (even-odd union) — both done; this is a NEW topology case.

ACCEPTANCE: a planar-eraser unit test (cut an angled stamp across a brush band -> 2 fills, x-extent == original) AND a merge-drawing-oracle / interactive e2e cutting a real brush line in two leaving two segments. NOTE per AGENTS.md: byte/unit not sufficient alone for the gesture — verify in the real editor that cutting a brush line yields two pieces.

Found by autonomous QA e2e agent at HEAD 5217287c0ced3b155a6fd6694866b18f6fdeaf07.
